test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

We walked (1) / beside the road (2) / and found shelter (3) / under a tree (4).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**beside**" in part (2) of the sentence.
 
• While "beside" means "next to" or "at the side of," the preposition "**along**" is more appropriate when describing movement (walking) that follows the length or direction of a path or road.
 
• In the context of traveling or walking, "**along the road**" is the standard idiomatic expression to indicate moving parallel to the road's course.
 
• Thus, the prepositional choice in **part 2** is the most suitable point of correction for better grammatical flow.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We walked **along the road** and found shelter under a tree."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beside vs. Besides:** A common confusion exists between these two. "**Beside**" indicates physical location (next to), whereas "**Besides**" means "in addition to" or "except for."
 
• **1: "We walked"** – This part is grammatically correct as a simple past tense construction.
 
• **3: "and found shelter"** – This correctly maintains the past tense consistency of the sentence.
 
• **4: "under a tree"** – This is the correct prepositional phrase used for seeking protection beneath an object.
